div.l: Vpon an ambler al esily she sat
Ywympled wel and on hir hede an hat
As brood as is a bokeler or a targe
A foot mantel aboute hir hipes large
And on hir feet a peyre of spores sharpe
In felawshipe wel cowthe lawghe and carpe
Of remedies of lowe she knewe ꝑparchaunce
For she cowthe of that art the olde daunce
A good man was there of Religioıı̄un
And was a poủere ꝑpersoıı̄un of a toıı̄un
But riche he was of holy thought and werk
He was also a lerned man and a clerk
And cristes gospell trewely wolde preche
His parisshens deuoutely wolde he teche
Benigne he was / and wonder diligent
And in adủersite ful pacient
And such he was pued ofte sithes
Ful loth were hym to curse for his tithes
But rather wolde he ȝeuen out of doute
Vn to his poủere parisshens a boute
Of his offryng / and of his substance
He cowthe in litel thyng haue suffisance
Wyde was his parissh / and houses fer assonder
But he ne lefte nought / for reyn ne thonder
In syknesse nor in meschief to visite
The ferthest in his parissh moche and lite
Vpon his feet / and in his honde a staf
This noble ensaumple vn to his sheep he ȝaf
That ferst he wroughte / and afterward he taughte
Out of the gospel . he tho wordes kaughte
And this figure / he added ther to
That ȝif gold ruste / what shal Iren do
For ȝif a preest be foul in whom we truste
No wonder is a lewed man to ruste
And shame it is ȝif a preest take kepe
A Shite Sheꝑperde and a clene shepe
Wel oughte a preest ensaumple for to ȝiue
By his clennes / how his sheep shulde liue
He sette nought his benefice to hire
